newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Volga-Dnepr to expand U.S. operations.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Volga-Dnepr to expand U.S. operations.

text.p: Russia's private Volga-Dnepr Airlines plans to expand its heavy cargo operations in the United States this year, a top company official said on Friday.
"There is big demand to carry such cargo in the United States," Alexei Isaikin, Volga-Dnepr chief executive, told a news conference. "Shipments of oil and gas equipment are very promising."
He also said that Ulyanovsk-based Volga-Dnepr planned to lease more Antonov-124 freighters this year.
The company set up aircraft maintenance posts last year in Sharjah, United Arabs Emirates, and in Shannon, Ireland.
Volga-Dnepr operates seven Antonov-124 planes, each with a capacity of 120 tonnes, three Ilyushin-76s, one Antonov-12 and one Antonov-32.
The company also operates a regular passenger route between Ulyanovsk, in central Russia, and Moscow, using a Yakovlev-40.

Volga-Dnepr boosted sales in 1996 to $111 million from $87.2 million in 1995, carrying 45,100 tonnes of cargo last year, compared to 39,633 tonnes in 1995. A company spokesman said that most of 1996's sales were made on An-124s.
"It gave us $101.4 million of our total sales volume," he said, adding that these aircraft carried 40,000 tonnes of cargo over 1996.
